title: Linking frass and insect phenology to optimize forest defoliation estimation
author: Thapa, Wolter, et al.
materials: to calculate total foliage biomass loss (kg·ha−
Box 1Instar Weighting Optimization Alt-text: Unlabelled box

steps.title: Establish Sampling Plots
steps.instruction: Establish variable-radius plots for the target defoliators (e.g., 26 plots for C. pinus in Wisconsin and 65 plots for L. dispar dispar in Maryland).

substeps.instruction: Create a central subplot and four satellite subplots arranged in cardinal directions.
Set the distance between the center subplot and satellite subplots to 25 m for C. pinus and 30 m for L. dispar dispar.

steps.title: Deploy Frass Traps
steps.instruction: Install frass traps (Tullgren funnels or laundry baskets with cotton sheets) with surface areas ranging from 1231.63 to 2370 cm².

substeps.instruction: For C. pinus: Place 4 to 6 traps in the outer one-third of the canopy footprint of host trees (selected using a metric factor 2 Bitterlich prism), with one trap in each satellite subplot and two in the center subplot.
For L. dispar dispar: Place 4 to 5 traps in the center plot at a distance of one-half to two-thirds between the stem and crown border of randomly selected host trees.

steps.title: Collect and Process Samples
steps.instruction: Collect frass and greenfall material based on species-specific intervals and process in the laboratory.

substeps.instruction: Collect C. pinus frass at approximately 7-day intervals.
Collect L. dispar dispar frass weekly, typically for 24-hour periods.
Sort deposited material in the lab to separate green foliage (greenfall) from frass.
Sieve the material to remove other detritus.
Oven dry both frass and greenfall at 55 °C for a minimum of 72 hours.

steps.title: Calculate Biomass and Deposition Rates
steps.instruction: Convert dry mass measurements into standardized area-based rates.

substeps.instruction: Scale dry mass of frass and greenfall to kg·ha⁻¹ based on the size of the frass traps.
Convert to a daily rate (kg·ha⁻¹·day⁻¹) by assuming an average deposition rate over the sampling period.
Average the rates across all traps to derive plot-level deposition rates.

steps.title: Estimate Ingested Biomass (IB)
steps.instruction: Calculate the actual amount of foliage consumed by larvae using the approximate digestibility (AD) of the species.

substeps.instruction: Use the formula: Ingested biomass (IB, kg·ha⁻¹) = frass (kg·ha⁻¹) / (1 − AD).
Apply AD = 0.30 for C. pinus and AD = 0.35 for L. dispar dispar.

steps.title: Calculate Total Foliage Biomass Loss
steps.instruction: Determine the total biomass loss by combining ingested biomass and greenfall.

substeps.instruction: Add the collected greenfall biomass (kg·ha⁻¹) to the estimated ingested biomass (IB).
Convert the result to foliage biomass loss per day (kg·ha⁻¹·day⁻¹).

steps.title: Determine Caterpillar Phenology
steps.instruction: Use BioSIM (V.11) to simulate life stages based on plot latitude, longitude, and weather station data.

substeps.instruction: Estimate the population percent within each larval instar for each day-of-year (DOY).
Identify the maximum number of instars: 7 for C. pinus; 5 for L. dispar dispar (male) and 6 for L. dispar dispar (female).

steps.title: Optimize Instar Weighting (w)
steps.instruction: Iteratively fit a distribution function to link BioSIM phenology data with field-collected frass/biomass data to determine the relative food consumption of each instar (L2 through the final instar).

substeps.instruction: Fit a distribution function to daily frass data to minimize the root-mean-square-error (RMSE) between fitted and observed frass.
Initialize the model with arbitrary instar weightings (w) to calculate 'weighted larvae' (sum of w × population proportion).
Iteratively re-fit until the difference between field-collected frass and fitted weighted larvae is minimized.
Validate using leave-one-out cross validation (LOOCV) and report RMSE and nRMSE.

steps.title: Impute Missing Data and Estimate Annual Biomass
steps.instruction: Fill gaps in field data and calculate total seasonal biomass loss.

substeps.instruction: Calculate a probability distribution curve of weighted instars for each DOY.
Use the cumulative density function of weighted larvae to impute frass or foliage biomass loss for missing days in the feeding window.
Validate the imputation using a K-week cross-validation procedure.
Sum the daily frass rates for the entire feeding season to estimate total annual frass biomass (kg·ha⁻¹).
